item.text:
**Verdict:** No.

Putin’s 2023 record is strongly negative on media freedom and information access. The strongest evidence shows censorship, criminal pressure on journalists and outlets, foreign-agent designations, propaganda, and punishment of antiwar or independent reporting. I did not find credible 2023 evidence that he protected independent media in a way that offset that pattern.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Short claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Russia: 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | [link](https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia) | The report says authorities further restricted media, forced NGO closures, jailed antiwar protesters and opposition figures, and opened 844 criminal cases for antiwar expression. It also says the “discrediting the military” laws were used widely and indiscriminately, which is direct evidence of censorship and pressure on information access. | 4B.6, 3B.8, 4B.3 |
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023) | Freedom House says the Kremlin maintains a controlled media environment, criminalizes dissent, and relies on a subservient judiciary and loyal security forces. That is direct evidence against protecting independent media. | 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.4 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Looking back at 2023, Freedom House says the regime intensified propaganda, used patriotic and militaristic narratives, and kept civic expression tightly constrained. That is strong evidence of disinformation and information control rather than press protection. | 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.3 |
| Russia designates The Moscow Times newspaper a “foreign agent” | Reuters | 18 Nov 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-designates-the-moscow-times-newspaper-a-foreign-agent-3238256) | Reuters reported that the Justice Ministry designated an independent newspaper a foreign agent, adding burdens and restrictions after it had already been blocked. This is a clear example of state pressure on independent journalism. | 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.3 |
| Russia’s anti-war media crackdown crosses new thresholds | Reuters | 21 Apr 2023 | [link](https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/analysisrussia-crosses-new-lines-in-crackdown-on-putins-enemies-2992615) | Reuters described security services and courts as crossing new thresholds in a campaign against perceived enemies, spies, and traitors. In context, this supports a broader pattern of intimidation that chilled independent reporting and civic information channels. | 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.3 |
| Putin called Wagner mutiny treason and promised punishment | Reuters Connect | 24 Jun 2023 | [link](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/moment-putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMucom,2023:newsml_VA240124062023RP1) | Putin’s own televised framing of the mutiny as treason shows the broader information environment he encouraged: loyalist, punitive, and hostile to alternative narratives. This is indirect, but it reinforces the propaganda/punishment pattern. | 4B.6, 4B.5, 3B.9 |

**Search gap:** I did not find credible 2023 evidence that Putin protected independent media or widened information access. The closest counterevidence was generic Kremlin rhetoric about dialogue or negotiations, but it did not amount to press freedom, media independence, or reduced censorship.
